input_text: On the issue of whether the defendant knew he was trespassing, the fact that he shook his head when asked by a passing security guard about whether he knew he was on private property.

extraction.input_text: On the issue of whether the defendant knew he was trespassing, the fact that he shook his head when asked by a passing security guard about whether he knew he was on private property.

claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The head shake occurred when asked by a passing security guard, making it an out-of-court communication rather than trial testimony.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(b) - A statement is one that is made other than while testifying at the current trial or hearing.
arguments.evidence_span: when asked by a passing security guard

arguments.text: Shaking one's head in response to a direct question demonstrates an intent to communicate, satisfying the assertion requirement under FRE 801(a)(2).
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(a)(2) - Conduct of a person, if it is the person's intent to communicate, constitutes a statement.
arguments.evidence_span: the fact that he shook his head when asked

arguments.text: The evidence is offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted—specifically, that the defendant knew he was on private property—to establish his knowledge for the trespassing charge.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c)(1) - A statement is hearsay if offered in evidence to prove the truth of the matter asserted in the statement.
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of whether the defendant knew he was trespassing

arguments.text: The evidence meets all three definitional prongs of FRE 801(c) (out-of-court, assertion, offered for truth), thereby classifying it as hearsay.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) - Definition of hearsay requiring all three prongs to be satisfied.
